# `silk/machine/snapshot`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The whole state of a running machine as one value, and the steps that advance it:
[`Snapshot`](#Snapshot) and [`Steps`](#Steps).

## When to use
Use [`Steps.begin`](#Steps.impl.begin) to start a machine and [`Steps.send`](#Steps.impl.send) to give it an event without
performing any effect, for example in a test. Use the `silk.machine.actor` module when the
effects must also be performed.

## Details
A [`Snapshot`](#Snapshot) holds the state value, the context, the queued events and effects, the clock and
the running timers. When the four types of the machine implement `Schema`, the snapshot does
too, so a program can write it as JSON, read it back and continue. Every time is `u64`
nanoseconds. [`Steps.advance`](#Steps.impl.advance) moves the clock and takes the delayed transitions that are due.

## Gotchas
A step that never settles, or that runs out of memory, leaves the machine with
[`Status.Failed`](#Status.Failed). It takes no more events after that.

Import as `Snapshot` with `import silk.machine.snapshot { Snapshot }`.

<a id="Steps.impl.begin"></a>

### Associated function `begin`

```silk
pub effect fn begin<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(context: C, now: u64) -> Snapshot<S, E, C, X>
    ! OutOfMemoryError | TransitionLoopError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the first snapshot of a machine: its initial state entered with `context` at the
wall clock time `now`, in nanoseconds. A machine without delayed transitions can pass 0.

<a id="Steps.impl.send"></a>

### Associated function `send`

```silk
pub effect fn send<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(
    snapshot: &mut Snapshot<S, E, C, X>,
    event: E,
  ) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError | TransitionLoopError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Processes `event` and everything it raises, and returns whether a state handled `event`.

#### Errors
`TransitionLoopError` when eventless transitions or raised events never settle, and
`OutOfMemoryError`. Either one leaves the machine `Status.Failed`, with its timers cancelled,
so it takes no more events. [`Steps.advance`](#Steps.impl.advance) fails the same way.

<a id="Steps.impl.nextDeadline"></a>

### Associated function `nextDeadline`

```silk
pub fn nextDeadline<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(snapshot: &Snapshot<S, E, C, X>) -> Option<
    u64
  >
```

Returns the deadline of the timer that fires first, in nanoseconds of wall clock time.

#### Details
It is the earliest of the machine's own timers and of [`Machine.deadline`](./machine-chart.md#Machine.deadline), which is how
the timers of a child machine are counted.

<a id="Steps.impl.advance"></a>

### Associated function `advance`

```silk
pub effect fn advance<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(
    snapshot: &mut Snapshot<S, E, C, X>,
    now: u64,
  ) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError | TransitionLoopError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Moves the machine's clock to `now` and takes the delayed transitions that are due, earliest
first. Returns whether one was taken.

#### Details
`now` is wall clock time in nanoseconds. A deadline is kept as it was set, so a timer whose
deadline passed while the program was not running fires on the first call after a restore.
When [`Machine.deadline`](./machine-chart.md#Machine.deadline) is due, [`Machine.tick`](./machine-chart.md#Machine.tick) runs one time after the machine's own
timers.
